paper.title: The Sampling Complexity of Condorcet Winner Identification in Dueling Bandits

unmapped: Only assumption on the preference matrix is the existence of a Condorcet winner (no transitivity)
settings.definition_quote: Given $\delta\in(0,1)$, the learner must output the CW $i^*$ with probability at least $1-\delta$ by adaptively and sequentially choosing pairs $(i,j)$ to be compared and choosing a stopping time. We evaluate an algorithm by its (random) number of duels $N_\delta$, called the \emph{budget}

unmapped: Only assumption on the preference matrix is the existence of a Condorcet winner (no transitivity)

unmapped: Goal: return a value between the d-th and u-th ordered arm means (up to epsilon), fixed budget
settings.definition_quote: given $N$ arms with means $(\mu_i)_{i\in [N]}$ ordered as $\mu_{(1)}\le\cdots\le\mu_{(N)}$ and indices $d<u$, it returns an estimate $\hat t$ that falls between the $d$-th and $u$-th means (up to an additive error $\varepsilon$)

algorithms.name: FB-CWI (Fixed Budget CW Identification, with certification)

symbols.H_cw: sum_{i != i*} 1/Delta_{i*,i}^2 (gaps of the Condorcet winner row)

source.label: thm:main_fb
source.quote: The output of Algorithm~\ref{algo:3} with input $T$, denoted $\psi_T$, satisfies \[ \mathbb{P}\left( \psi_T \neq i^*\right) \le 27K\log(K)\log(T) \cdot\exp\left(-c_1\cdot\frac{T}{\log(T)\log(K)H_{\text{cw}}}  \right), \] where $c_1$ is a numerical constant.

results.notes: Restated as Theorem thm:amain1 in the appendix.

bound.regime: for any s with 1 <= s_i <= K_{i;<0}

symbols.H_certify: sum_{i != i*} 1/Delta_{i,(s_i)}^2, Delta_{i,(s)} the s-th most negative entry of row i of the gap matrix

conditions: s_i <= K_{i;<0} (number of negative entries in row i)

source.label: thm:main_fb
source.quote: Moreover, for any $\bm{s}$,  we also have \mathbb{P}\left( \psi_T \neq i^*\right) \le 47K\log(K)\log(T) \cdot\exp\left(-\frac{c_2}{\log^3(K)\log(T)}\cdot \frac{T-c_3\cdot H_{\text{explore}}^{(0)}(\bm{s})\log^{5}(H_{\text{explore}}^{(0)}(\bm{s}))}{H_{\text{certify}}(\bm{s})+H_{\text{explore}}^{(1)}(\bm{s})}  \right), where $c_2$ and $c_3$ are numerical constants.

results.notes: Holds for every s simultaneously (bound can be minimized over s). Restated as Theorem thm:amain2.

symbols.H_tradeoff: min over s with s_i <= K_{i;<0} of (H_certify(s) + H_explore1(s))*log(1/delta) + H_explore0(s)

source.label: thm:fc2
source.quote: There exists a constant $c_0$ such that the following holds for any $\delta \in (0,1/6)$. Under the assumption of the existence of a CW, the output of Algorithm~\ref{algo:fc} ... satisfies $\mathbb{P}(\psi_{\delta} \neq i^*) \le \delta$. Moreover, the total number of queries $N_{\delta}$ ... satisfies, with probability at least $1-\delta$, N_{\delta} \le \tilde{c}\cdot (...) where $\tilde{c}$ is proportional to $c$ and hides logarithmic factors in $K$ and $(\Delta_{i,(1)})_{i\neq i^*}$ and a $\log\log(1/\delta)$ factor.

results.notes: Algorithm is delta-correct; budget bound holds w.p. >= 1-delta. Log factors in K, Delta_{i,(1)} and loglog(1/delta) hidden.

symbols.Delta_i1: Delta_{i,(1)}: most negative entry of row i of the gap matrix (gap to the strongest opponent of arm i)

conditions: gap matrix entries in [-1/4,1/4], skew-symmetric, with a Condorcet winner

source.label: thm:LB_exp_instance_first_regime
source.quote: Let $K \geqslant 2$ and $\delta \in (0,1/6)$ and consider any gap matrix $\bDelta\in\mathbb{D}_{\mathrm{cw}}$. For any algorithm $A$ that is $\delta$-correct on $\mathbb{D}_{\mathrm{cw}}$, the budget $N_{\delta}$ satisfies \mathbb{E}_{\bDelta,A}[N_{\delta}] \geqslant \frac{1}{4} \sum_{i\neq i^*} \frac{\log\!\left(1/(4\delta)\right)}{\Delta_{i,(1)}^2}

symbols.Delta_i1: Delta_{i,(1)}: most negative entry of row i of the gap matrix

conditions: gap matrix entries in [-1/4,1/4], skew-symmetric, with a Condorcet winner
results.notes: Lower bound on the (1-delta)-quantile of the budget: budget exceeds the value with probability at least delta.

symbols.G_i: K_{i;<0}/||Delta_i^-||_2^2: number of negative entries of row i over squared l2 norm of its negative part

conditions: algorithm is delta-correct for CW identification on D_cw
Delta has no ties (Delta_{i,j} != 0 for i != j)
holds on a permuted instance tilde Delta in D(Delta) with the same negative entries per row

source.label: thm:LB_hp_instance
source.quote: Let $A$ be a $\delta$-correct algorithm for CW identification, with $\delta \leqslant 1/12$, and let $\bDelta\in \mathbb{D}_{\mathrm{cw}}$. Assume that $\bDelta$ has no ties ... one can construct a matrix $\tilde \bDelta$ by permuting the entries of $\bDelta$ ... such that \mathbb{P}_{\tilde{\bDelta},A}( N_{\delta} \geqslant \frac{1}{3}\max_{i\ne i^*}\frac{K_{i;< 0}}{\|\Delta_i^-\|^2}\log(\frac{1}{6\delta}) \vee \frac{1}{37 \log(2K)}\sum_{i \ne i^*}\frac{K_{i;< 0}}{\|\Delta_i^-\|^2}) \geqslant \delta.

results.notes: Lower bound on (1-delta)-quantile of the budget on a permuted instance. A more general version with ties (Theorem thm:precise_LB_high_proba, constants 1/(8 log(4/3)) and 1/(128 log(4/3) log(2K)), with K_{i;<=0}) is in the appendix.

symbols.H_certify_star: sum_{i != i*} 1/Delta_{i,(s_i*)}^2 at the optimal effective sparsity s*

conditions: algorithm is delta-correct for CW identification on D_cw
local minimax: holds for some tilde Delta in D(Delta) (same CW, same effective sparsity s*, same gaps Delta_{i,(s_i*)})

source.label: coro:Lower_bound_minimax
source.quote: Let $A$ be a $\delta$-correct algorithm for CW identification, with $\delta \leqslant 1/12$, and let $\bDelta\in \mathbb{D}_{\mathrm{cw}}$. Then, one can construct $\tilde\bDelta\in \mathbb{D}(\bDelta)$, such that \mathbb{P}_{\tilde{\boldsymbol{\Delta}},A}\left(N_{\delta}\gtrsim H_{\text{certify}}(\bm{s}^*,\delta)+H_{\text{explore}}(\bm{s}^*,\delta)\right)\geqslant\delta, where $\gtrsim$ hides a log term in $K$ and a numerical constant.

results.notes: Lower bound on (1-delta)-quantile of the budget; hides log K factor and constants.

conditions: worst case over permutations preserving the CW row (uniform (1-delta)-quantile tilde chi)

source.label: thm:precise_LB_high_proba_tilde
source.quote: Let $A$ be a $\delta$-correct algorithm over $\mathbb{D}_{\mathrm{cw}}$, with $\delta\leqslant1/12$. Let $\boldsymbol{\Delta}\in\mathbb{D}_{\mathrm{cw}}$ have no ties. ... Then, \tilde{\chi}\geqslant\frac{1}{16\log(4/3)}\max_{i\neq i^*}\left(\frac{1}{\Delta_{i^*,i}^2}\wedge\frac{K_{i;<0}}{\|\Delta_i^-\|^2}\right)\log\!\left(\frac{1}{6\delta}\right)

results.notes: tilde chi is the worst-case (over CW-row-preserving permutations) (1-delta)-quantile of the budget.

symbols.Delta_cw_i: Delta_{i*,i}: gap of the Condorcet winner against arm i

conditions: worst case over permutations preserving the CW row
results.notes: Delta-independent term of the quantile lower bound.

symbols.H_cw: sum_{i=2}^K 1/Delta_i^2 for the prescribed CW gap vector

conditions: max over the class D^(1)(underline Delta) of gap matrices built from a vector with Delta_1 = 0 and Delta_i in (0,1/4)

source.label: thm:LB_exp_minimax_first_regime
source.quote: Let $K \ge 2$ and $T\in \mathbb{N}^*$ and  consider any vector $\underline{\Delta}$ with $\Delta_1=0$, and $\Delta_i\in(0,1/4)$ for $i\ne 1$. For any algorithm $A$ with a fixed budget $T$, one has \max_{\bDelta \in \mathbb{D}^{(1)}(\underline{\Delta})} \mathbb{P}_{\bDelta, A}\left( \hat{i}_T \neq i^* \right) \ge \frac{1}{4}\exp\!\left(-22 \frac{T}{H_{\mathrm{cw}}}\right)

results.notes: Local minimax fixed-budget lower bound; exact definition of D^(1) is in the omitted appendix.

conditions: max over class D^(2)(underline Delta, underline s) with Delta_1=0, Delta_i in (0,1/4), 1 <= s_i <= K/4

source.label: thm:LB_minimax_H2
source.quote: Let $T\in\mathbb{N}^*$, $K$ a multiple of $8$, ... Then, any fixed-budget algorithm $A$ satisfies \max_{\boldsymbol{\Delta}\in\mathbb{D}^{(2)}(\underline{\Delta},\underline{s})}\mathbb{P}_{A,\boldsymbol{\Delta}}(\hat{i}_T\neq i^*(\boldsymbol{\Delta}))\geqslant\frac{1}{4}\exp\!\left(-5\frac{T}{\max_{i=2}^{K/2}\frac{K}{s_i\Delta_i^2}}\right).

symbols.Delta: common gap value Delta_i = Delta for i in {2..K/2}

conditions: Delta_i = Delta > 0 and s_i = s in [K/4] for i in {2,...,K/2}
max over class D^(2)(underline Delta, underline s)

source.label: thm:LB_minimax_H2
source.quote: If, additionally $\Delta_i=\Delta>0$ and $s_i=s\in[K/4]$ for all $i\in\{2,\dots,K/2\}$, then \max ... \geqslant\frac{1}{4}\exp\!\left(-10\frac{T\Delta^2}{K}\right)

results.notes: Delta here is the paper's common row gap, used in the canonical 'uniform gap' sense.

conditions: Delta_i = Delta > 0 and s_i = s in [K/4] for i in {2,...,K/2}
max over class D^(2)(underline Delta, underline s)
results.notes: Implies K^2/(s Delta^2) samples needed for constant success probability.

source.label: thm:conj
source.quote: Consider Algorithm~\ref{algo:inter} with inputs $(K, d, u, T)$, such that $u>d$. Then, the output satisfies for any $\epsilon\in (0,1)$: \mathbb{P}\left( \hat{t}^{(2)}_{\bar{\ell}} \notin [\mu_{(d)}-\epsilon, \mu_{(u)}+\epsilon] \right) \le 40\log_2(T)\exp\left(-c \cdot r \cdot \frac{\epsilon^2T}{\log\!\left(\frac{16K}{u-d}\right)\log_2(T)}\right)

results.notes: Noise model assumed bounded (Bernoulli duels in the application); epsilon is not an input of the algorithm. Corollary cor:quant specialises to d=ceil(K/8), u=ceil(K/4): log(T)exp(-c eps^2 T/log T).
